summary: Arsema G Food Mart LLC is an operating Ethiopian and Eritrean grocery at 6667 W Washington St, verified as a physical walk-in storefront by two owner calls, current daily hours, a working store line, and a USDA SNAP authorization at the premises. Its Google presence is duplicated: two live listings share the address, the phone (317) 603-3274 and the same website — 'Arsema Food Mart', filed as a convenience store with 4.5 stars across 8 reviews, and 'Ethiopian Eritrean Store', filed correctly as a grocery store with 5.0 across 22 reviews and a description naming injera, berbere, shiro, spices and coffee. The business's 30 reviews are split between the two listings and no owner response is displayed on any of them. Yelp and BBB carry no record of the business at all; the Facebook page that exists publishes the correct address and a contact email but is small (12 followers) and carries no website or phone. The owned web presence is a Square Online subdomain whose shop states plainly that items are not yet available for sale. The primary opportunity is consolidating one duplicated Google identity into a single claimed, correctly-categorized listing and putting the imported assortment — the store's differentiator — where customers can see it.
public_narrative: Arsema G Food Mart is an Ethiopian and Eritrean grocery store on West Washington Street in west Indianapolis, serving the city's East African community. The market carries imported pantry staples — injera, berbere, shiro, teff, spices and coffee — alongside fresh meat, African goods and cultural items, and it accepts SNAP/EBT. Open daily from 10:00 AM to 9:30 PM, the store is a walk-in neighborhood market for customers shopping for the ingredients of Habesha cooking.

digital_opportunity_score.rationale: Google maintenance scores 1 rather than 2 because one listing carries owner-provided elements (a description, a 'From the business' section and highlights), so substantial neglect is not verified — but the profile is split across two listings and the one bearing the business's own name carries the wrong primary category and no description. Review response scores the maximum 3: 30 of 30 observable reviews across the two listings display no owner response. Unanswered negative reviews score 0 — no review at or below 3 stars was observed. Website scores 1: the storefront is live and secure with a built cart, but its catalog carries no sellable items and its copy does not name the assortment. NAP scores 1 on verified material inconsistencies — a second live trading name at the same address, a conflicting registered address, and three phone numbers in circulation.

gap_analysis.summary: The verified gaps concentrate on one problem with several faces: the business's identity is split across two live Google listings, so its category, description and reviews are divided, and its name is attached to the weaker half. Beyond Google, the business is absent from Yelp and BBB, its Facebook page omits the website and phone, and its owned storefront is scaffolded but empty. The registered-versus-storefront address difference and the multiple phone numbers are the category-typical dual-address pattern rather than errors in themselves, but they need one canonical value chosen and propagated.

outreach_problems.problem: Customers find two different store names at one address — and the listing with the bigger review base and the right category is not the one carrying the store's own name.
outreach_problems.regular: I noticed Google lists your store twice at 6667 W Washington — once as Arsema Food Mart filed under convenience store, and again as Ethiopian Eritrean Store — and your customer reviews are split between the two.
outreach_problems.hook: Look up your own address on Google sometime: it shows two different stores at 6667 W Washington, and most of your reviews sit on the one that doesn't say Arsema.
outreach_problems.solution: Settle on one storefront name, claim that listing, correct its primary category to the African grocery shelf, and merge or retire the duplicate so every review, photo and link lives under one identity — then make sure the same name, address and phone appear on every directory that currently carries a variant.
outreach_problems.evidence: Two live Google listings sharing 6667 W Washington St and (317) 603-3274: Arsema Food Mart (Convenience store, 4.5 across 8 reviews, plus code PPVF+P9) and Ethiopian Eritrean Store (Grocery store, 5.0 across 22 reviews, plus code PPVF+PC).
outreach_problems.outreach_use: Cold-call opener or first-touch email — the duplicate is verifiable in one search and the owner can confirm it in thirty seconds.

outreach_problems.problem: Thirty customers have left five-star reviews and not one has a reply from the store — the goodwill is there but nothing shows the owner is present.
outreach_problems.regular: You have thirty reviews across the two listings, almost all five stars, and none of them has a response from you. Replying is the cheapest way to show new customers the store is run by someone who cares.
outreach_problems.hook: Thirty people took the time to write that your injera and your shelves are the best around — and none of them heard back. That's thirty conversations left on the table.
outreach_problems.solution: Claim the surviving listing and work through the existing reviews with owner responses, then set a habit of replying to each new one — starting with the recent reviewers who named the owner and the staff by name.
outreach_problems.evidence: Thirty observable reviews across the two Google listings (8 + 22) at 4.5 and 5.0 stars, with zero owner responses displayed on any of them; observable response rate 0 percent.
outreach_problems.outreach_use: Second touch or objection response — concrete, checkable, and it lands hardest after the duplicate finding because the reviews are the asset being split.

outreach_problems.problem: A customer who checks beyond Google finds nothing — no BBB record, and the Facebook page that exists doesn't carry the store's phone or website.
outreach_problems.regular: Outside Google, the trail goes cold: there's no BBB record for the store, and the Facebook page has your address and hours but no phone number or website on it.
outreach_problems.hook: Try to call your store from your own Facebook page — the number isn't there, and there's no BBB record for a business that's been importing direct for years.
outreach_problems.solution: Build the missing second sources: add the phone and website to the Facebook About, align its hours with Google's, and establish a BBB record — each populated with the same name, address, phone and hours as the consolidated listing.
outreach_problems.evidence: Operator sweep found no Yelp or BBB listing for either trading name; the Facebook About publishes the address, hours, an email and Messenger, but no phone and no website; Facebook hours read 11:00am - 9:30pm against 10:00 AM - 9:30 PM on Google and Waze.
